channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic Prices at $83 a Share in Record-Sized Offering
item.description: Anthropic PBC and its co-founders raised $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement. The artificial intelligence firm sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders sold 23.6 million shares for $83 each, according to a statement, above the marketed range. The IPO is the biggest of all time, topping SpaceX’s $75 billion base deal. Sopnendu Mohanty, Group CEO of Global Finance and Technology Network, discusses some of the risks associated with the valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Korea Investors Buy Record Amount of Treasuries in September
item.description: South Korean investors bought a record amount of US Treasuries in September, a sharp reversal after dumping an unprecedented volume of the securities earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Hooyeon Kim and Masaki Kondo

item.title: Jeffrey Sachs Expects Friendly Trilateral Outcome
item.description: Columbia University Professor Jeffrey Sachs says he is happy that the leaders of US-China and Russia have agreed to have a trilateral meeting. Speaking to Bloomberg’s Stephen Engle, he adds that his expectations are that the outcome will be ‘calm’ and ‘friendly’. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Oil Imports Rebound as Beijing Turns Back to Stockpiling
item.description: China’s appetite for crude is recovering faster than expected in the final months of 2026, as lower oil prices push cash-strapped refiners to use up government-granted import allowances and encourage processors to rebuild stockpiles depleted by months of war.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Trade and AI Rivalry to Dominate APEC Summit
item.description: Bloomberg's Stephen Engle reports from Shenzhen where he breaks down the key topics likely to play out during a trilateral meeting between President Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Speaking to Bloomberg, Columbia University Professor Jeffrey Sachs also argues that the US cannot win a trade war with China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-Google Engineer May Face New Charges Over Bets on Gemini 3.0
item.description: A former Google software engineer accused of making an illegal bet on Polymarket about company search data may face additional charges that he also traded on the release date of its Gemini 3.0 artificial-intelligence model.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch and Daniele Lepido

item.title: Seesaw Day for Markets, Anthropic IPO Looms
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Doubleline’s Global Sovereign and Emerging Markets Head Bill Campbell, Csis’ Senior Fellow Henrietta Levin, Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler, Omni Federal’s General Manager of AI and Edge Jana Eggers, Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management’s Executive Director Katerina Simonetti, Willkie Farr and Gallagher’s Capital Markets Practice Co-Chair Edward Best, Citi’s Chair and CEO Jane Fraser, Salesforce’s Former AI CEO Clara Shih, Harbor Capital Advisors’ Portfolio Manager Justin Menne. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jane Fraser on IPO Pipeline, AI, & Interest Rate Outlook
item.description: Jane Fraser, Citi's Chair and CEO, says NVIDIA’s better-than-expected earnings and increased guidance were not the only issues investors were weighing; they were also focused on whether AI-related financing would continue and who would lead the company next. She speaks with Lisa Abramowicz at Bloomberg Newsmakers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Steadies Near 14-Month Low as Fed Signals More Rate Hikes
item.description: Gold steadied near a 14-month low after hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials reinforced expectations for interest-rate hikes stretching into next year.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 19
item.description: Oil steadied after slumping on Wednesday, as traders assessed the outlook for the next phase of the US-Iran conflict.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Lorelei Smillie

item.title: Bain Pushes Back LNG Glut Outlook to 2030 as War Tightens Market
item.description: A looming global glut of liquefied natural gas has been pushed back by more than a year as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts supplies and delays projects, according to Bain & Co., extending a period of tightness that’s delivering higher profits for traders.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Stapczynski

item.title: Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler Warns Anthropic’s Cash Flow Poses Big Risk To AI Economy
item.description: Gary Gensler, former SEC Chair and Professor of the Practice of Global Economics and Management and Finance at MIT Sloan School of Management, joined Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick about Anthropic and OpenAI’s corporate governance structure, the evolving role of the SEC, and risk factors he’s watching. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Skydance Skips FIFA World Cup Bid as Netflix, Fox Eye $4 Billion Deal
item.description: Skydance Corp. is opting out of bidding for the US media rights for the next FIFA Men’s World Cup tournaments in what could be one of the costliest and competitive auctions in the global soccer event’s history, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Miller

item.title: Eddie Best on Expectations for Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: Edward Best, co-chair of Wilkie Farr & Gallagher’s capital markets practice, discusses Bloomberg’s report that Anthropic may price its IPO at $83 per share, up from an initial marketing price of $70. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brookfield-Backed Lotto Firm Logs Earnings Hit, Buys Back Bonds
item.description: Earnings at Brookfield-backed lottery business Scientific Games Holdings LP fell in the last quarter, hurt by one-time costs related to delayed contract completions, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Weinman and Dorothy Ma

item.title: Citi CEO Looks Forward to Working With Sen. Warren
item.description: Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser says she is ready to work with Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, who has been critical of the bank. She speaks to Lisa Abramowicz at a Bloomberg Newsmakers event in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Stock Futures Climb on Anthropic IPO Pricing: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures advanced after Anthropic PBC priced its initial public offering above the marketed range, putting investor appetite for the technology sector to a fresh test following recent losses.
item.dc:creator: Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Probe of Mark Walter’s Insurers Spotlights Gaps in Regulatory Patchwork
item.description: Trinidad Navarro knows how to hunt down wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Alex Rajbhandari and David Voreacos

item.title: Chicago’s Third CFO This Year Saw Red Flags Before Exit
item.description: The sudden departure of Chicago’s third chief financial officer in a year came after she repeatedly raised concerns about budgeting practices, including inconsistent deficit calculations.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Date Singh

item.title: Bitcoin Erases Bessent Rally as Leverage and Liquidity Fade
item.description: Bitcoin has erased all the gains from its late-summer rally as fading risk appetite and the record hack at exchange Binance drove investors to retreat, leaving the largest token trading in a thinner market increasingly vulnerable to sharp price swings.
item.dc:creator: Sidhartha Shukla
